Posted October 22, 2002
Special to MarijuanaNews

Yesterday in Vancouver, there was an administrative hearing on the cases involving Steve Tuck, Steve Kubby, Renee Boje, and Ken Hayes.

The hearing was held with a representative of the Canadian Minister of Immigration present.

Tuck, who represented himself because he could not afford an attorney, reported that the minister indicated that the decisions would be made on the validity of their medical need for cannabis, not on political concerns about Washington. In fact, I suspect that the prohibitionist threats against Canadian/DEAland trade have backfired.
See
Walters Concedes That Canada Can Legalize Cannabis If It Wants To, Which Was The Only True Thing He Said While In Montreal.

In any case, Canadian law prohibits the deportation of refugees who would face torture or death if they are deported. Obviously, if the Canadian government recognizes that a refugee needs cannabis to avoid a painful death, then it would be impossible for Canada to deport them to the United States.

Steve Kubby has already been given a medical exemption based on the recognition that his life depends on access to cannabis. Under such a circumstance, how could the same government say that it would be acceptable to send him back to DEAland?
See
Walters Puts The Media to the Test By Taking Hyper-Lying to A New Level. Blood Libels To Justify Police State. San Diego Medical Activist Faces Federal Charges for 20 Plants.

So far, it has been impossible for Steve Tuck to get access to Canadian specialists who are qualified to understand the extraordinary nature of his back injuries and the numerous surgeries which have been done. He will now be able to have a hearing where he will be allowed to call expert witnesses. This also means that he is safe in Canada now for at least a year.

The bad news is that he is going to need significant funding to be able to defend his life. Consequently, within the next week I am going to help organize a defense fund for Steve. He is an extraordinary American who deserves the support of the cannabis community, and from everyone who cares about freedom.

I am very proud to have him as a friend. Moreover, his case raises many other important points about the cannabis issues, not only in Canada, but also in DEAland. His is a story that must be told.

It is quite clear that there are elements in the Canada government, especially in Health Canada under the prohibitionist Anne McLellan, who oppose medical cannabis because they are both ignorant and beholden to the police state.
See
Cruelty, Incompetence, And Quackery Threaten Canadian Medical Cannabis Patients.

For their own reasons, they want to argue these cases on medical grounds, but so do the supporters of medical cannabis in the Canadian government. The result is that the battle will be fought on the merits of the case for medical cannabis. We know that freedom has nothing to fear from the truth.

Hannah Arendt explained the advantage that we have over the prohibitionists when she wrote, The trouble with lying and deceiving is that their efficiency depends entirely upon a clear notion of the truth that the liar and deceiver wishes to hide. In this sense, truth, even if it does not prevail in public, possesses an ineradicable primacy over all falsehoods.

Most Canadian prohibitionists clearly do not understand the truth about medical cannabis, so they do not even lie about it very well.
See
Canadians Need to Examine The Role of the Police In Maintaining Marijuana Prohibition. Paying For Lies That Distort Public Policies and Undermine Sovereignty. Analysis by Richard Cowan

Bear in mind that the constitutional challenges to Canadian cannabis prohibition will finally be argued before its Supreme Court in December, with a ruling expected in the 2nd half of next year.
See
Extraordinary Editorial in Winnipeg Free Press Outlines " Findings of Fact " In Possession Case to Be Heard by Canadian Supreme Court.

Also the Canadian government has indicated that it will support some form of decriminalization in Parliament, presumably early next year. I am not hopeful about them passing an honest decrim bill.
See
The Agenda for the Prohibitionist Counterattack in Canada. Analysis by Richard Cowan

Nonetheless, the stage is set for a multi-front battle in 2003. The cases involving the refugees will be an important part of that struggle with major implications for cannabis prohibition in DEAland.

When Steve's friends have worked out the details of the defense fund, I will post the information on MarijuanaNews.com
